checks.name: 28/28 status-code and content-negotiation probes behave as designed
JSON and JSON-LD of the same URL are both valid JSON with different media types
count == 1,391 and default page size is 50
walking all pages gives every CVE exactly once, equal to the clean KEV table
page_size is capped at its maximum (asked 100,000)
first page has previous=None, last page has next=None
techniques: 799 distinct ids == attack_technique table
tactics: 14 rows; CWEs: 176 rows
no filter and ?search= of a CVE id: client.count() works without downloading everything
16/16 filters return exactly the pandas set (no duplicates, count() agrees)
?ordering=-date_added is non-increasing over all pages
?ordering=-n_mappings: first row has the maximum number of PKEV mappings
techniques: ?ordering=-n_vulnerabilities gives the technique with most CVEs; subtechnique filter and tactic filter work
1,391 CVE detail documents are identical to the clean tables (KEV, NVD, CWE, PKEV, evidence, tactics)
missing != empty: CVEs without CVSS v3.1 show cvss_v31 = null (not 0, not empty)
972 CVEs have attack == [] (= not mapped by PKEV) and 419 have mappings
799 technique detail documents are identical to the clean tables (incl. parent, sub-techniques, tactics, CVEs)
the CVE view and the technique view describe the same 1,183 mappings
all 1,391 JSON-LD documents use only terms defined in the @context (nothing would be dropped)
one context term per IRI (otherwise expand->compact could rename keys)
every document carries the same @context as /api/context/ and as jsonld.CONTEXT
@id of every CVE is its NVD IRI; of every technique its attack.mitre.org IRI
graph: 1,391 vulnerabilities, 1,183 mapping nodes, 155 distinct techniques (same as pandas)
graph: mappings per mapping_type == pandas value_counts
datatypes: all dateAdded are xsd:date, all CVSS scores xsd:decimal
missing != empty: no empty-string literal anywhere; CVSS v3.1 node only for the 1,389 CVEs that have one
three-way: CRITICAL CVEs mapped to an initial-access technique — SPARQL on JSON-LD == REST filter == pandas
PyLD expand->compact round trip returns the document unchanged (29 CVEs incl. the 2 without CVSS)
each sampled document parses alone with rdflib (self-contained @context) and gives > 10 triples
facts read back from the JSON-LD graph (id, mappings, techniques, CWEs) == the JSON of the same CVE
same @id in two documents -> one node in the merged graph, with the properties of BOTH (vulnerability link from the technique doc; technique + capabilityGroup from the CVE doc)
merged graph is smaller than the sum of the two (shared nodes are not duplicated)
4 upstream sources with commit and data-file SHA-256 == config/sources.yaml (NVD has 1,391 files: no single hash, by design)
dataset carries the raw-manifest and cleaning-code SHA-256 of the Phase-2 manifest (covers all 1,391 NVD files)
9 clean tables listed with SHA-256 == Phase-2 manifest and rowCount == rows in the database
dataset document is valid JSON-LD (no undefined terms) and parses as a dcat:Dataset with 4 prov:wasDerivedFrom
every dcat:accessURL answers 200 in every advertised media type (the metadata does not lie)
list queries do not grow with page size (5 vs 200 rows): vulnerabilities and techniques
detail queries are constant (<= 12) whatever the number of mappings / references
latency sanity: every request type has a median below 1 s on the local dev server

one PKEV mapping removed -> reported
ransomware flag flipped -> reported
invented evidence URL -> reported
technique loses a CVE -> compare_technique reports it
context without 'cveId': undefined_terms flags it
the same broken context makes a JSON-LD processor DROP the triple SILENTLY (no error)
two terms for one IRI ('cveId' and 'ident') -> terms_sharing_an_iri flags it
extra key 'foo' in a document -> undefined_terms flags it
